Hi Karen —

Thanks for sending this over and flagging the two points. High-level reactions below; saving Karthik and Laura in case legal/procurement want to weigh in with precise redline language.

1) Notice window: We can be flexible on notice windows at the order form level. For the MSA framework, our standard is a mutual 60-day notice for termination for convenience only where both parties can terminate the applicable Order Form(s). For operational predictability we prefer (a) order forms to carry 30-day notice when tied to seat/commit volume, and (b) MSA-level termination to be scoped to material breach or insolvency.

2) Auto-renew: We understand Acme's desire to avoid surprise renewals for pilots. Proposal: pilot and evaluation order forms can be set to not auto-renew; production order forms will include an auto-renew option with a 30-day opt-out window before renewal. If Acme needs no auto-renew at all, we'll need to discuss pricing/commit impacts.

Attached a short internal memo that outlines the commercial impacts (RW_MSA_Response_20260210.pdf). Karthik — can you propose redline text for the MSA and one-sentence language for a pilot carve-out?

If that sounds workable, I'll coordinate with Acme to get updated redlines back for counter-signature.

Hi all —

I've reviewed Acme's redlines and Steph's note. Below are concrete redline suggestions we can send back; I've kept the language tight to limit downstream risk: 

1) Termination for convenience (MSA-level): We are willing to permit termination for convenience at the MSA level with 60 days' written notice, provided the terminating party pays for (a) any non-refundable pre-paid capacity and (b) a pro rata charge for committed but undelivered services for the notice period. Recommended clause: "Either party may terminate this Agreement without cause upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other party; termination under this Section shall not relieve the terminating party of payment obligations accrued prior to the effective date of termination, and Customer shall be responsible for any prepaid or committed amounts covering the notice period."

2) Termination for convenience (Order Form level / Pilots): For pilot or evaluation Order Forms, we agree to a non-auto-renewal approach by default (no auto-renew), and either party may elect to terminate the pilot Order Form without penalty upon thirty (30) days' notice. Production Order Forms shall default to automatic renewal for successive one-year terms unless Customer provides notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days prior to the renewal date.

3) Auto-renew opt-out mechanics: Add an explicit opt-out window and a requirement that Redwood send a renewal notice at least 45 days before the renewal date to remind Customer of upcoming auto-renew.

Track-change snippet attached (RW_termination_redlines.txt) for legal to paste into the MSA. If Acme is comfortable with the payment-for-notice construct and the pilot carve-out, I think we're at a place to exchange final redlines and proceed to signature.

I'll be available for a call this afternoon if you want to walk the language.

Thanks,
